title: SM Entertainment Reports Revenue Decline On Lower Music Sales, Concert Revenue
summary: The K-pop label said it had fewer major releases in the quarter "as our major artists focused on expanding their overseas activities."
body: SM Entertainment’s stock sank more than 7% on Wednesday (Nov. 4) after the label home of K-pop stars aespa and NCT reported an unprofitable quarter. The company said lower physical and digital music sales and concert revenue resulted in a 9% decline in overall revenue. SME said it generated 291.1 billion Korean won ($205.2 million) in revenue and operating profit of 35.5 billion Korean won ($25 million), which is down 26% from the year-ago quarter. The company operated at a net loss of 1.1 billion Korean won ($775,000) for the quarter, down from a 44.7 billion Korean won ($31.5 million) profit a year ago, “primarily due to foreign exchange-related losses resulting from the appreciation of the Korean won,” Jeongmin Jang , CIO of SM Entertainment, said on a conference call discussing the quarter. title: Bluetooth’s next big audio upgrade is coming, but not to your current devices
summary: Standardizing lossless and high-res audio.
body: TL;DR The Bluetooth SIG has announced HDT, a new technology that raises Bluetooth LE’s maximum bit rate from 2Mbps to 7.5Mbps. The optional Bluetooth Core 7.0 feature also promises better energy efficiency and more reliable connections across devices. Existing devices won’t automatically gain support, but the first compatible audio products could arrive in 2027. Qualcomm’s FastConnect 8800 already advertises HDT support. The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG), the standards organization that oversees Bluetooth technology, today shared a significant update that could standardize lossless and high-resolution Bluetooth audio . It announced the adoption of Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT), which essentially increases Bluetooth LE’s maximum supported bit rate to 7.5Mbps. That’s nearly four times the current maximum. For the regular user, this should eventually mean much wider access to lossless and high-resolution audio over Bluetooth in future wireless earbuds and headphones.

Meanwhile, industry sources say the ongoing RAM crisis could continue until 2029 or 2030. The RAM crisis, driven by rising demand for AI infrastructure, has pushed prices up across the board, including smartphones. So far this year, Google and Samsung have raised prices, while other OEMs have been forced to make trade-offs to avoid that fate. But a RAM shortage may not be the only issue brands face heading into 2027, as Samsung’s OLED screens, which are used by several phone makers, could also become pricier. According to Chinese supply chain source ChannelGate, Samsung has told its suppliers that the cost of OLED panels will rise in 2027 by around $10 to $20 (via ITHome ). The source adds that this hike isn’t due to price-related pressures, but a company strategy to “regain control” of OLED panel pricing, which Samsung supposedly feels is “chaotic” right now.

body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority There’s no arguing that smartphone cameras have gotten really good. In fact, I believe that there are no bad cameras as far as flagships go, just different flavors. Sure, bigger sensors and better lenses help, but the key differentiator today is the processing, color science, and the level of control you get over images. To that effect, I spent the past month shooting with the iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro to see how their newfangled approaches to creative control compare. On the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple has reworked its Photographic Styles, giving you more control over the look and texture of your photos. Two instances of thick-film chip resistor cracking were observed during thermal cycling after vibration, with fractures occurring across the short axis due to bending. Failure analyses ruled out defective lots and fatigue, identifying board flexure, component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses as contributing factors.
